title: Chapter 227: Help! Help!
html:
“You go ahead. I’ve heard this Haunted House divides its scenarios into several difficulty levels. We rarely get the chance to visit the hardest one, so I want to explore a little longer.” Ye Xiaoxin remained inside the director’s office.

The recorder’s white noise grew louder, and other sounds began to surface within it—ragged breathing and muffled sobs.

Han Qiuming checked the time. They had two minutes left, and he could not afford to linger. “All right. Take care of yourself.”

He turned toward the exit with the recorder. As his back receded into the darkness, Ye Xiaoxin—who had remained composed throughout the visit—stared after him, eyes wide. Why is someone clinging to his back?

Ye Xiaoxin did not believe in the supernatural; that was why she could review so many Haunted Houses without fear. Yet she had just witnessed something her experience could not explain. Who was that on his back? One of the workers?

…

Han Qiuming sprinted through the corridor with the recorder. Two minutes left!

His body temperature plummeted. A chill radiated from his back, spreading through his body until it pierced his heart.

“Pain…”

A voice brushed past his ear, there and gone in an instant.

“Who said that?” Han Qiuming looked over his shoulder. He had the distinct sensation of a girl clinging to his back, yet nothing was there. “Did I imagine it?”

He ran faster, driven by the simple desire to escape. “I have the item. The moment I get out, I win. I’ll restore Tian Teng Medical School’s reputation!” Ignoring everything else, Han Qiuming dashed onward.

“So painful…”

The voice drew closer, drifting from his back to his ear as though trying to burrow inside.

“So painful!”

“Ahhh!” Han Qiuming angrily flailed at the empty air. “Come out! Who are you?”

No one answered. Only the echoes of his voice and the tape’s white noise filled the long corridor.

“Is it the recorder?” Apart from him, it was the only possible source. Han Qiuming held it before his eyes. The tape was still turning, and the light above the play button had changed from green to red. “It has to be!”

Han Qiuming could not determine what was wrong, and time was running out. Gritting his teeth, he clutched the recorder and resumed his desperate sprint. Something is definitely wrong with it, but it’s also the key to clearing the scenario! We spent so long finding it—I’m not throwing it away and wasting all that effort!

Han Qiuming cursed Chen Ge inwardly. How despicable!

To win, he had to escape with the tape recorder. Abandoning it meant defeat, but keeping it meant enduring its torment. No normal person could clear a scenario like this.

“Argh!” Han Qiuming clenched his teeth, ready to risk his life to clear Chen Ge’s Haunted House. He kept running, but the weight on his shoulders steadily increased. Something seemed to be pressing down on him, its chill seeping into his bones.

“So painful…”

The voice behind him grew clearer. What had begun as an indistinct murmur had become a woman’s voice—one that sounded strangely familiar, filled with helplessness and despair.

Wait a minute!

Every hair on Han Qiuming’s body stood on end. I’ve heard this voice before.

His sanity began to fracture. Somehow, in a Haunted House he had never visited, he had encountered a familiar voice. Where did I hear it?

Cold sweat trickled down his forehead. He had few female friends, and almost none his own age. No, I’ve definitely heard it somewhere!

A memory from half a year earlier surfaced. While redesigning Tian Teng Medical School to make the attraction more compelling, he had ignored everyone’s objections and insisted on incorporating the deaths of Xu Zhenzhen and her father into the story. In pursuit of authenticity, he had researched Xu Zhenzhen extensively.

The young woman had worked at her father’s hospital before being dismissed over a medical error. The patient’s family had caused an enormous scene, and a video of the confrontation had even appeared online. They had gone to the hospital demanding an explanation from Xu Zhenzhen. Wearing her nurse’s uniform, she had stood surrounded by doctors and nurses, explaining herself in a soft voice while no one listened. The situation had spiraled out of control. She had been shoved to the floor, and someone had even stepped on her fingers.

“So painful…”

Yes! This is the voice!

Han Qiuming’s head felt ready to explode. Inside a Haunted House, he was listening to the voice of a dead victim.

He hurled the recorder away. Even if he had ten lives to spare, he would never approach it again.

Why is Xu Zhenzhen’s voice on that tape? Did that Chen fellow do this? Impossible! He couldn’t have known we would visit the Third Sick Hall. I was the one who suggested changing the plan.Han Qiuming wanted to slap himself across the mouth. I never should have said anything!

The recorder came from Tian Teng Medical School. Could the real Xu Zhenzhen—the woman whose story I exploited—have returned as a ghost?

His temperature continued to fall, leaving his skin cold, while the pressure on his shoulders intensified. I have to get out first. This place is far too haunted.

Han Qiuming kept running, but after only a few steps, he was gasping desperately for air. The soft mattresses offered no purchase, and his body seemed to grow heavier with every stride.

What’s going on? It feels like I’m carrying something.

Han Qiuming looked back. Cushioned by the mattresses, the recorder lay unharmed where he had thrown it, its tape still turning. The spinning reels resembled a peculiar smile—or a whirlpool meant to draw him in.

I need to escape.

The tape recorder was far behind him, yet its white noise seemed to hiss directly into his ears.

“So painful, so painful…”

The woman’s voice flooded Han Qiuming’s mind, driving a crazed light into his eyes. “Stop talking! I told you to stop!”

He punched at the air and spun wildly, searching for the source. For an instant, he saw a woman’s face resting on his shoulder, whispering into his ear.

“I’ve got you now!” He switched on his phone’s flashlight and aimed its camera behind him. As the view turned, a familiar face—one he had seen countless times in newspapers and medical records—appeared on the screen. “Xu... Xu Zhenzhen!”

The phone slipped from his hand, and Han Qiuming fled down the corridor. His body grew colder, and the voice refused to release him.

“So painful, so painful, so painful!”

Han Qiuming rounded the corner and returned to the wreckage of the mannequins. Oblivious to the changes among them, he charged forward blindly. He knew he had watched his footing, yet something caught his ankle and sent him sprawling amid the scattered bodies. His thick glasses flew from his face.

“My glasses!”

Han Qiuming crawled on all fours. The world had become a blur, but he could still distinguish the shapes of hands, legs, and heads. He reached for his glasses, only for them to slide away as though the mannequins were passing them along.

In the darkness, he sensed countless heads and limbs creeping toward him.

“What are you?! Don’t come any closer! Help! Help!”
